tips.title: Check the age, education and attempt limits before you commit: each route has its own authority and its own notification
tips.cost: No cost. An hour with the official notifications saves an application fee and a wasted year.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no single ladder of pathways with one age band. Each route is run by a different authority and each notification sets its own limits. The National Defence Academy admits unmarried candidates aged 16.5 to 19.5 who are in or have passed class 12. The Agniveer scheme takes candidates aged 17.5 to 21. The Combined Defence Services examination is for graduates. The UPSC Civil Services Examination needs a bachelor's degree, and for the general category an age of 21 to 32 with six attempts. State public service commissions, the Staff Selection Commission, teaching through the Central Teacher Eligibility Test and the state tests, and open schooling and open universities through NIOS and IGNOU all set their own conditions, and the reserved categories get age relaxation. Self-employment has no age or qualification limit at all.
tips.benefit: Read the notification, not a coaching brochure. The Civil Services Examination requires a bachelor's degree, allows candidates aged 21 to 32 in the general category, and limits them to six attempts, with relaxations for the reserved categories, ex-servicemen and persons with disabilities. The National Defence Academy entry is for unmarried candidates aged 16.5 to 19.5, and physics, chemistry and mathematics are needed for the Air Force and Navy wings. Agniveer recruitment is open to candidates aged 17.5 to 21 with the educational qualification the trade requires. State public service commissions and the Staff Selection Commission publish their own age bands and post-wise qualifications. Teaching needs a qualification recognised by the National Council for Teacher Education plus the Teacher Eligibility Test, and the Central Teacher Eligibility Test is conducted by the CBSE. NIOS and IGNOU admit learners to secondary, senior secondary and degree programmes under open schooling and open university rules, and both have eligibility conditions rather than entrance competition.
tips.sources: Union Public Service Commission. <https://upsc.gov.in/>; Staff Selection Commission. <https://ssc.gov.in/>; Indian Army recruitment. <https://joinindianarmy.nic.in/>; National Council for Teacher Education. <https://ncte.gov.in/>; National Institute of Open Schooling. <https://www.nios.ac.in/>; Indira Gandhi National Open University. <https://www.ignou.ac.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A because every limit here is printed in a government notification, but the notification for your cycle is what counts. Age is counted on a cut-off date the notification names, not on your birthday. Keep the certificate, the mark sheet and the category certificate ready; a mismatch between the name on the certificate and the application is one of the commonest reasons a candidature is rejected. This item covers eligibility only, not which route suits you, and no coaching institute can change a published rule.

tips.title: India has no compulsory military registration and no draft: joining the armed forces is voluntary, and each service publishes its own age limits
tips.cost: No cost to apply. Enlistment itself is a multi-year commitment during which you cannot hold another job.
tips.inPlainWords: No Indian law requires a young person to register for military service. There is no draft, no annual registration deadline and no penalty for not joining. Entry is voluntary and competitive: the National Defence Academy and the Combined Defence Services examination through the UPSC, Agniveer recruitment through the Army, Navy and Air Force, and direct recruitment by the Indian Coast Guard. Women have been admitted to the National Defence Academy since 2022 (the Supreme Court's August 2021 order opened the examination to them). If you do not apply, nothing happens; if you apply and are not selected, nothing happens either.
tips.benefit: Compare the routes on their own terms. The National Defence Academy takes candidates aged 16.5 to 19.5 after class 12 and trains them for three years before a commission. Agniveer is a four-year engagement open to candidates aged 17.5 to 21; at the end a proportion is retained in the regular cadre and the rest leave with a Seva Nidhi package and a skill certificate. The Combined Defence Services examination is the graduate route and is conducted twice a year. The Indian Coast Guard recruits Naviks and Assistant Commandants directly. The three services also recruit technical and trades entries through their own notifications. Every one of these is advertised on a government website, and the medical and physical standards are printed in the notification.
tips.sources: Union Public Service Commission, National Defence Academy and Combined Defence Services examinations. <https://upsc.gov.in/>; Indian Army recruitment. <https://joinindianarmy.nic.in/>; Indian Navy. <https://www.indiannavy.nic.in/>; Indian Air Force. <https://afcat.cdac.in/>; Indian Coast Guard. <https://www.indiancoastguard.gov.in/>; Ministry of Defence. <https://www.mod.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A because the absence of conscription is a matter of statute and practice, and each route's terms are published. The rules on age, marital status, tattoos, eyesight and physical standards differ by entry and are enforced strictly at the medical examination; a candidate rejected on medical grounds can appeal to the appellate medical board named in the notification. Anyone who offers to reserve a seat for a fee is committing a fraud, because recruitment is free. Service is disciplined employment with restrictions on political activity and outside business, so read the terms before you apply.

tips.title: Backing out after enlistment is a disciplinary matter under service law, not a civil penalty: desertion is an offence, and a short commission ends on its stated date
tips.cost: No fee. The cost is the decision itself: a short commission ends on the date it states, and leaving before that date is an offence. Read the terms before you sign.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no scheme of fines, travel bans or education bans for someone who declines military service, because there is no compulsory service to decline. Once a person has enlisted the relationship is governed by the Army Act 1950, the Navy Act 1957 and the Air Force Act 1950, which make absence without leave and desertion offences triable by court martial. An officer on a short service commission leaves when the commission ends, with no penalty and no bar on study or foreign travel. For those who leave early, the consequence is disciplinary and, where a bond was signed, recovery of training costs.
tips.benefit: The practical difference matters when you compare India with countries that conscript. There is no government list of draft evaders, no exit ban and no bar on sitting a civil service examination for someone who never applied. What exists is the service law that binds a person who has enlisted: the Army Act 1950, the Navy Act 1957 and the Air Force Act 1950 set out offences including absence without leave, desertion and insubordination, and each service runs its own court-martial procedure. A short service commission runs for the term stated in the commission, usually with an option to apply for a permanent commission, and an officer not selected for a permanent commission is released at the end of the term with a release certificate. Where a cadet leaves training before commissioning, the academy rules and the bond signed at admission apply, and a bond can require recovery of training costs.
tips.sources: Army Act, 1950. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Navy Act, 1957. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Air Force Act, 1950. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Defence. <https://www.mod.gov.in/>; Indian Army recruitment. <https://joinindianarmy.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A on the legal position, but the disciplinary detail is service-specific and this book does not quote the punishment scales. The bond signed at admission to a service academy is a contract and the amount is in that document, not here. A person who is released or dismissed should keep the release order, because it determines pension, gratuity and later re-employment rights. Nothing in this item is advice to leave or to stay.

tips.title: Enlisting does not pay your tuition: the Indian benefit is the Agniveer Seva Nidhi package, a skill certificate and preference in later police recruitment, while study is funded through NSP and education loans
tips.cost: No application fee for the scholarship portal or the loan portal. Enlistment pays a salary, not a tuition refund, and the four-year engagement is the price.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no scheme that reimburses a student's tuition in exchange for enlisting. An Agniveer is paid a salary during a four-year engagement and leaves with a Seva Nidhi package, part of it contributed from pay, plus a skill certificate; a proportion is retained in the regular cadre. For study itself the routes are the National Scholarship Portal, which carries central and many state scholarships, and the Vidya Lakshmi portal, which lists education loans from banks, with the PM Vidyalaxmi scheme providing collateral-free loans with a credit guarantee for students admitted to eligible institutions.
tips.benefit: An Agniveer is enrolled for four years, receives a monthly salary, and on exit receives the Seva Nidhi package, built from the individual's own contribution and a matching government contribution, together with a skill certificate for the training completed; a proportion of each batch is retained in the regular cadre on merit. The Ministry of Home Affairs has announced reserved vacancies and age relaxation for ex-Agniveers in the central armed police forces and the Assam Rifles, which is the clearest employment benefit attached to the scheme. For study, the National Scholarship Portal is the single window for central schemes such as the central sector scholarship for college students and for many state schemes, and the income limits, deadlines and documents are set out there. The Vidya Lakshmi portal lets a student compare education loans from several banks on one application, and the PM Vidyalaxmi scheme gives a credit guarantee so that a loan for an eligible institution needs no collateral.
tips.sources: Ministry of Defence, Agniveer scheme. <https://www.mod.gov.in/>; Indian Army recruitment. <https://joinindianarmy.nic.in/>; National Scholarship Portal. <https://scholarships.gov.in/>; Vidya Lakshmi education loan portal. <https://www.vidyalakshmi.co.in/>; Ministry of Education. <https://www.education.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A because each element is published by a ministry or the scheme, but the Seva Nidhi amount and the retention quota are fixed by the scheme in force in your recruitment year, so read that year's notification. A reserved vacancy in a police force still requires passing the recruitment test, and age relaxation moves the upper limit rather than guaranteeing a post. Scholarship income limits and deadlines change every year, and a late application is simply rejected. An education loan must be repaid: the credit guarantee removes the collateral, not the debt.

tips.title: Discharge does not come with a government job: the Indian route is reservation in central and state posts, resettlement training through the DGR, and health cover through the ECHS
tips.cost: No fee for the resettlement courses, the ESM card or the pension. The effort is registering with the record office and the Zila Sainik Board, which most people do late.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not guarantee a job on discharge. What exists is a set of entitlements: reservation of a share of central civil posts for ex-servicemen under the Ex-Servicemen (Re-employment in Central Civil Services and Posts) Rules, similar quotas in many state services, resettlement training and job fairs run by the Directorate General of Resettlement, and lifetime health cover through the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme. The Rajya Sainik Board and the Zila Sainik Board are the local offices that handle the papers.
tips.benefit: An ex-serviceman's re-employment rights rest on three things that have to be claimed. First, the Ex-Servicemen (Re-employment in Central Civil Services and Posts) Rules reserve a share of vacancies in the central civil services and posts, and many states run their own quota in state services and the police; the roster is published by the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare. Second, the Directorate General of Resettlement runs resettlement courses, from security-guard and fire-safety training to management courses, and organises job fairs; the courses are subsidised and are the reason to register early rather than after the money runs out. Third, the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme gives contributory lifetime health cover through empanelled hospitals, and the ESM card is the identity that these benefits are keyed to. The Rajya Sainik Board and the Zila Sainik Board verify the papers.
tips.sources: Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare. <https://www.desw.gov.in/>; Directorate General of Resettlement. <https://www.desw.gov.in/>; Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme. <https://www.echs.gov.in/>; Ministry of Defence. <https://www.mod.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A because the rules and the institutions exist and are published, but no rule gives an ex-serviceman a specific post. The reservation operates through a roster in a recruitment cycle, so a person who registers late may find the cycle closed. Register with the Zila Sainik Board and get the ESM card before discharge where possible. The quota does not replace the qualification the post requires, and a person appointed under it serves on the same terms as anyone else. If a department refuses to apply the roster, the grievance goes to the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare through the Rajya Sainik Board.

tips.title: After discharge, check the pension, gratuity, ESM card and re-employment routes before the money runs out
tips.cost: ECHS is a contributory scheme. A resettlement course is free or subsidised.
tips.inPlainWords: A person leaving the armed forces should check the pension or the one-time gratuity, the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme, the ESM identity card and the re-employment and resettlement courses. The entitlement depends on the years of service and the rank. Visit the nearest Zila Sainik Board or the Directorate of Ex-Servicemen Welfare, and keep the discharge book and the PPO.
tips.benefit: The pension and gratuity rules for the armed forces are set by the Ministry of Defence. The Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme covers the veteran and the family at empanelled hospitals. The Zila Sainik Board provides the ESM card and the resettlement help. The Directorate General of Resettlement runs courses and job fairs. A short-service commission has a different entitlement from a pensionable commission.
tips.sources: Ministry of Defence. <https://www.mod.gov.in/>; Directorate of Ex-Servicemen Welfare. <https://desw.gov.in/>; Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme. <https://echs.gov.in/>; Kendriya Sainik Board. <https://ksb.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A pension is not automatic if the record is incomplete. Apply for the PPO and the ECHS card early. A private job offer should be checked before you accept it.

tips.title: There is no ten per cent quota for grassroots service in India: the route into government is the examination, an apprenticeship or a contract post, plus the category relaxations
tips.cost: No fee for most central applications, though state examinations charge a small fee. The trade-off is time: an examination cycle runs about a year, and a contract post pays a contract salary.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no scheme that sets aside a share of government vacancies for people who have completed a two-year rural service programme, and no bonus marks in a postgraduate entrance test for that service. The routes are the examinations themselves: the UPSC civil services and the state public service commissions, the Staff Selection Commission for central Group B and C posts, and the relaxations that come with a caste, disability or ex-serviceman certificate. Apprenticeships under the Apprentices Act 1961 and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme give training and a stipend without a job guarantee, and national health programmes hire contractual staff on fixed-term terms.
tips.benefit: Understand what each route actually gives. The Civil Services Examination and the state public service commission examinations are open competitions with published syllabi, a preliminary stage and a mains stage, and the reserved categories get a lower cut-off and additional attempts where the rules allow. The Staff Selection Commission recruits for central Group B and C posts on the same principle. Apprenticeship is governed by the Apprentices Act 1961 and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme shares the stipend with the employer; an apprenticeship is training and creates no right to a post, though a completed apprenticeship is a recognised qualification. National health programmes, the National Health Mission in particular, advertise contractual posts for nurses, laboratory technicians and programme managers on fixed-term contracts renewed subject to the programme. Volunteering through the National Service Scheme or the Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan builds a record but carries no placement entitlement.
tips.sources: Union Public Service Commission. <https://upsc.gov.in/>; Staff Selection Commission. <https://ssc.gov.in/>; Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, apprenticeship. <https://www.msde.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A on the routes, because each is a published recruitment system, but a foreign grassroots-quota scheme does not transfer: anyone promising a reserved government seat after two years of social work in India is misrepresenting the rules. A contract post can end when the programme or its funding ends, so do not take on a long lease on the strength of one. Category certificates must be in the prescribed format and, for a central examination, issued by the competent authority. Read the advertisement's essential qualification line before buying study material.

tips.title: Teaching is a recognised qualification plus a teacher eligibility test plus a recruitment examination: no scheme turns three years of contract teaching into a permanent post
tips.cost: The D.El.Ed or B.Ed course costs money, and so does the examination fee. The trade-off is time: a two-year qualification, then the eligibility test, then a recruitment cycle that may not come every year.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no programme that guarantees a permanent teaching post after three years of service. What is required is a qualification recognised by the National Council for Teacher Education, a pass in the Teacher Eligibility Test, and then selection in the state's teacher recruitment examination. Guest teachers, contract teachers and para-teachers are hired on fixed terms and their service does not by itself convert into a permanent post. The Central Teacher Eligibility Test is conducted by the CBSE for central schools, and each state runs its own test.
tips.benefit: The chain has four links, and missing one is why applications are rejected. First the qualification: the National Council for Teacher Education prescribes the minimum qualifications for a primary and an upper-primary teacher, and a degree from an unrecognised institution does not count. Second the eligibility test, which section 23 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 makes a condition of appointment, is run by the CBSE as the Central Teacher Eligibility Test and by each state as its own test, and a pass is valid for the period stated in the notification. Third recruitment: states advertise vacancies and hold a written examination, often with weight for the eligibility test score, and publish a merit list. Fourth appointment: the selected candidate is posted by the state on the state's pay scale for the post, not at a contract rate. Guest and contract teachers are paid from a different head and stand outside this chain, which is why their years of service do not count towards permanence.
tips.sources: National Council for Teacher Education. <https://ncte.gov.in/>; Central Board of Secondary Education, Central Teacher Eligibility Test. <https://ctet.nic.in/>; Ministry of Education. <https://www.education.gov.in/>; Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. <https://www.education.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A because the qualification and test requirements are statutory, but recruitment cycles vary and some states have run no regular teacher recruitment for years. No national rule converts contract service into a permanent post; a state that has such a scheme created it by its own order. Keep the eligibility test certificate, the D.El.Ed or B.Ed mark sheet and proof that the institution is recognised, because the last is checked and a degree from a non-recognised college is a common reason for rejection. An appointment in a private school is a contract with that school, not a government post.

tips.title: Fire and rescue, the central armed police and the Coast Guard are separate recruitments with their own tests and lower entry thresholds than the civil services
tips.cost: No fee for most central recruitments, though some state forces charge one. The process runs through a physical test, a written paper and a medical examination over several months.
tips.inPlainWords: India's fire and rescue services are run by states and municipal bodies, not by a single national force, so recruitment is advertised by the state fire service or the municipal corporation. The central armed police forces recruit constables and sub-inspectors through the Staff Selection Commission and their own boards, and the Indian Coast Guard recruits Naviks and Assistant Commandants directly. Defence civilian posts are filled by the department that holds them or through the Staff Selection Commission. None of these needs a bachelor's degree for the entry grade, and all of them test physical standards that are printed in the advertisement.
tips.benefit: Each route has a published standard. A state fire service recruits firefighters through its own advertisement, usually requiring class 12 and a physical efficiency test, with a written paper and a medical examination; the fire service is a state subject, so the pay scale and the age band are the state's. The central armed police forces recruit constables for general duty through the Staff Selection Commission, which publishes the age band, the physical standards and the written paper, and recruit assistant commandants through the UPSC. The Indian Coast Guard runs its own recruitment for Navik general duty and for assistant commandants, and prints eligibility and physical standards in each advertisement, while defence civilian Group C posts are advertised by the department that holds them. The common structure is a physical test, a written examination and a medical examination, and a candidate eliminated at the physical stage cannot compensate with a written score.
tips.sources: Staff Selection Commission. <https://ssc.gov.in/>; Union Public Service Commission, Central Armed Police Forces. <https://upsc.gov.in/>; Indian Coast Guard. <https://www.indiancoastguard.gov.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; Ministry of Defence. <https://www.mod.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A on the existence and structure of the routes, but the age bands, physical standards and pay scales differ by state and by year, so the advertisement is the only authority. A firefighter's job carries genuine physical risk, which is why the medical standards are strict. Do not pay an agent: each of these recruitments is advertised on a government website and the application is made there. A written result is not an appointment until the medical examination and the character verification are complete.

tips.title: A degree later in life is normal: NIOS for school-level certification and IGNOU or a state open university for a degree, recognised under UGC regulations
tips.cost: Fees are set by the institution and are modest compared with a private college; the real cost is the years of study while working. NIOS and IGNOU publish their fee structure, so check it before enrolling.
tips.inPlainWords: There are three legitimate routes for someone who missed higher education at 18. NIOS lets you complete secondary and senior secondary schooling through open schooling, with examinations through the year. IGNOU and the state open universities offer degree programmes through open and distance learning. The University Grants Commission recognises open and distance learning and online programmes under its regulations, so a degree from a recognised programme is a real degree for a government examination, though a few posts require a regular mode and say so in the advertisement.
tips.benefit: NIOS is a national board under the Ministry of Education: it admits learners to the secondary and senior secondary courses and to vocational courses, and its senior secondary certificate is accepted for admission to higher education and for many government posts. IGNOU is a central university and the state open universities are established by state law, and their degrees are awarded like any other university degree; the UGC regulations on open and distance learning and online programmes set the recognition conditions, and a programme outside them is not a valid degree. The practical difference from a regular college is the mode of study, not the standing of the qualification. For a government examination, read the advertisement: most accept any recognised degree, and the few that require a regular mode say so explicitly.
tips.sources: National Institute of Open Schooling. <https://www.nios.ac.in/>; Indira Gandhi National Open University. <https://www.ignou.ac.in/>; University Grants Commission, open and distance learning. <https://www.ugc.gov.in/>; Ministry of Education. <https://www.education.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A on the routes, but check two things before paying: whether the programme is recognised by the UGC in the current cycle, and whether the post you want accepts a distance degree. Keep every mark sheet and the final certificate, because a missing semester mark sheet can hold up verification for months. Fast-track degrees and unapproved foreign universities are sold as equivalents and are not; the UGC publishes the list of recognised universities. These courses take years, and no route avoids the examinations.

tips.title: Without an employer, you must arrange your own pension and health cover: NPS, PPF and a health policy
tips.cost: A monthly contribution and a health premium. The NPS charges a fund-management fee.
tips.inPlainWords: A self-employed person has no employer contribution. The main routes are the National Pension System, the Public Provident Fund and a health insurance policy. The NPS gives a tax deduction and a retirement corpus; the PPF is a safe long-term saving; a health policy covers hospital costs. Start early; a late start means a larger contribution for the same pension.
tips.benefit: The PFRDA regulates the NPS, and the PPF is a government small-saving scheme. A health policy is regulated by the IRDAI, and the premium depends on age and cover. The Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY covers an eligible household. The EPF is available only through a covered employer. The Income-tax Act gives a deduction for the NPS and the PPF within the limits.
tips.sources: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority. <https://www.pfrda.org.in/>; National Pension System. <https://www.npscra.nsdl.co.in/>; National Savings Institute, PPF. <https://www.nsiindia.gov.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A health policy has a waiting period for a pre-existing condition. The NPS tier-I is locked until 60. Do not rely on a single product.

tips.title: Gig work brings no per-order injury premium from the platform: your cover is the Code on Social Security 2020, e-Shram registration, a state welfare board and a personal accident policy
tips.cost: e-Shram registration is free. A personal accident policy costs a few hundred rupees a year; the platform's own cover, where it exists, is limited and conditional.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not require a platform to pay an occupational injury premium for every order a delivery rider or driver completes. What exists is weaker and worth knowing: the Code on Social Security, 2020 recognises gig workers and platform workers and provides for a Social Security Fund and contributions from aggregators, the e-Shram portal registers unorganised workers including gig workers, some states have set up welfare boards and Rajasthan has passed a law for platform-based gig workers, and a personal accident policy is the cover most workers actually rely on. Employees' State Insurance applies where there is an employer-employee relationship and the wage ceiling is met.
tips.benefit: Read the Code and the schemes. The Code on Social Security, 2020 defines a gig worker and a platform worker, provides for a Social Security Fund, and enables contributions from aggregators for the welfare of platform workers; the schemes under it are notified by the central and state governments, so what you receive depends on whether your state has notified one. Registration on e-Shram gives an unorganised worker a universal account number and access to the schemes and insurance linked to it. Rajasthan's Platform Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act, 2023 created a welfare board and a fund financed by a fee on transactions, and other states have announced boards of their own. Where the platform provides insurance, the policy wording decides what is paid, and most cover accidental death and hospitalisation rather than loss of income. A personal accident policy bought directly is the predictable layer.
tips.sources: Code on Social Security, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/>; e-Shram. <https://eshram.gov.in/>; Employees' State Insurance Corporation. <https://www.esic.gov.in/>; Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A on the legal framework, but the benefits are not uniform: a rider in one state may have a welfare board and a rider in the next may have nothing. Keep the e-Shram registration and the universal account number card. If a platform deducts an insurance premium from your payout, ask for the policy document; a deduction without a policy is a wage issue. An accident while riding for an app is often excluded from a personal accident policy that asks about occupation, so disclose the work when buying. For a dispute with a platform over pay or injury, the labour department of the state is the first office, not the police.

tips.title: There is no national six-year service bond: state medical colleges attach bonds to MBBS seats, and teaching requires a recognised qualification, with the terms set by each state
tips.cost: The bond is real money. A state medical college prospectus states the bond amount and the penalty for not serving, and the amount differs by state and by year. Read the prospectus before you accept a seat.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no nationwide scheme in which the government pays for a teacher's or a doctor's training in exchange for six years of service. What exists is state-specific: many state governments attach a bond to MBBS and postgraduate seats in government medical colleges, requiring the graduate to serve in a rural or government hospital for a stated period or to pay a penalty, and the terms are printed in the admission prospectus. Teaching has no bond of this kind; the requirement is a qualification recognised by the National Council for Teacher Education and a pass in the Teacher Eligibility Test, and where a state runs a sponsored teacher-training scheme, its own order applies.
tips.benefit: Take the two professions separately. For medicine the bond is a contract between the student and the state: a government medical college seat may carry an obligation to serve in a rural area or a government hospital for a stated number of years, with a penalty if the obligation is not met, and the amount and the period are in the prospectus issued for that year's admission. Because the terms are set by the state they cannot be generalised, and a candidate should read the prospectus of the college where the seat is offered before paying the fee. For teaching, the National Council for Teacher Education prescribes the minimum qualification and the Teacher Eligibility Test is a condition of appointment under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act; no national bond attaches to a D.El.Ed or B.Ed. Some states run sponsored training schemes with a service condition, and those are governed by the state's order.
tips.sources: Ministry of Education. <https://www.education.gov.in/>; National Council for Teacher Education. <https://ncte.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>; National Medical Commission. <https://www.nmc.org.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A on the framework, but no single figure can be given for the bond because each state sets its own, and this book will not invent one. A bond is enforceable, and a candidate who breaks it can be required to pay, with some states recovering the amount before releasing certificates. Ask the college for the bond text, not a summary from a senior student. Teaching has no bond, but a state-sponsored course may carry a service condition, so read that order too.

tips.title: Before working abroad, check that the recruiter is registered under the Emigration Act and use the eMigrate portal
tips.cost: A registered agent's fee is regulated. Do not pay a large 'placement' fee in cash.
tips.inPlainWords: Only a registered recruiting agent can recruit an Indian worker for a job abroad, and the agent must use the eMigrate system. An unregistered agent who charges a fee and sends you on a tourist visa is breaking the law and putting you at risk. Check the agent's registration on the eMigrate portal and the emigration clearance for your category before you pay.
tips.benefit: The Emigration Act, 1983 regulates the recruitment of Indian workers for employment abroad. The eMigrate portal lists the registered recruiting agents and processes the emigration clearance. A worker on a tourist visa cannot legally take a job. The Indian mission can help if the employer confiscates the passport or fails to pay, but prevention is better.
tips.sources: Ministry of External Affairs, eMigrate. <https://www.emigrate.gov.in/>; Emigration Act, 1983. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of External Affairs. <https://www.mea.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A job offer with no written contract and no employer details is a red flag. Keep the passport; no employer has the right to hold it. Register with the mission after you arrive.

tips.title: Remote work for a foreign employer is taxed where you live: the residency test decides it, and no one withholds the tax for you
tips.cost: No fee to file. A chartered accountant's fee is a real cost if you use one, and advance tax falls due in instalments during the year rather than in one payment at the end.
tips.inPlainWords: For Indian tax purposes the question is where you are resident, not where the payer sits. Under the residence test in the Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaced the 1961 Act on 1 April 2026 and renumbered its sections, you are resident if you are in India for 182 days or more in the tax year, or for 60 days in the year and 365 days in the four preceding years (the 60-day test does not apply to a citizen who leaves India for employment abroad or as a member of the crew of an Indian ship), and a citizen who is not liable to tax in any other country and whose income other than foreign sources is above fifteen lakh rupees is deemed resident under section 6(7); a visiting citizen or person of Indian origin above that threshold uses 120 days instead of 60. A resident is taxed on worldwide income, including salary paid abroad for work done in India, and a foreign employer has no Indian withholding obligation, so you pay advance tax during the year and file a return by the due date. The money arrives as a foreign inward remittance and the bank records a purpose code and issues a foreign inward remittance certificate.
tips.benefit: The mechanics are worth learning before the first payment arrives. Residency under the Income-tax Act, 2025 is tested on days of physical presence, and a resident is taxed on global income, so a salary paid into a foreign account for work performed from India is taxable here, while a non-resident is taxed only on income sourced in India. Because the foreign employer does not deduct tax at source, the liability is discharged through advance tax in the instalments set under the Act and reconciled in the income-tax return, and interest applies to short payment and to deferred instalments. On the remittance side, a receipt for services is a current-account transaction under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, and the bank records a purpose code and issues a foreign inward remittance certificate on request, which is the document a lender or a visa officer will ask for. Where the same income is taxed in another country, a double taxation avoidance agreement and the foreign tax credit rules apply, and the credit is claimed in the return.
tips.sources: Income-tax Act, 2025 (in force from 1 April 2026; replaces the 1961 Act). <https://www.incometax.gov.in/>; Income Tax Department. <https://www.incometax.gov.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, foreign exchange. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Central Board of Direct Taxes. <https://www.incometax.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A on the statutory tests, but this is not tax advice for your facts: the 60-day test, the deemed-residency rule in section 6(7), which catches an Indian citizen who is not liable to tax anywhere else and whose Indian income exceeds fifteen lakh rupees, and the treatment of an allowance each change the answer, and a chartered accountant should apply them. Keep the contract, the invoices and the bank advice, because proving the income and its nature is your burden. Do not split remittances to stay under a reporting threshold, since structuring is itself something the bank and the tax department look for. If you move abroad, the residency test changes and so does the return you file.

tips.title: Borrowing to start a business: MUDRA, the credit guarantee for micro and small enterprises, Stand-Up India and the PMEGP are the government-backed routes, and none of them is free money
tips.cost: No fee to compare schemes, and these loans are designed to need no collateral. The loan is still a loan and interest accrues from the day it is disbursed.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not subsidise half the interest on a startup loan as a general rule. The government-backed routes are different in kind: MUDRA loans for micro-enterprises through banks and microfinance institutions, the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises, which guarantees a collateral-free loan so the lender's risk is covered, Stand-Up India for a first-time borrower from the scheduled castes, scheduled tribes or a woman entrepreneur, and the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme for a manufacturing or service micro-enterprise. Eligibility, the ceiling and the interest rate come from the scheme and the lender, and a bank can refuse an application on its own credit assessment.
tips.benefit: Understand what each scheme does. A MUDRA loan is given by a bank, a regional rural bank, a cooperative bank or a microfinance institution under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana, categorised by the size of the loan, and the lender assesses the proposal. The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises does not lend: it gives a guarantee to the lender for a loan to a micro or small enterprise, which is what allows the loan to be sanctioned without collateral, and the guarantee cover has limits and a fee. Stand-Up India is for a first-time borrower in the scheduled castes, scheduled tribes or a woman entrepreneur, for a greenfield enterprise in manufacturing, services or the trading sector. The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme gives margin money support for a new micro-enterprise, with the rate depending on the category of the applicant. In every case the bank sanctions the loan, and a refusal can be taken up through the branch grievance mechanism and the scheme's nodal office.
tips.sources: MUDRA. <https://www.mudra.org.in/>; Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises. <https://www.cgtmse.in/>; Stand-Up India. <https://www.standupmitra.in/>; Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. <https://www.msme.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A on the existence and structure of the schemes, but the amounts, interest rates and support rates are revised, so the current guidelines and the sanction letter are what bind. No scheme makes borrowing safe: a loan has to be repaid from the business, and a personal guarantee signed by a spouse is a personal liability. A credit guarantee protects the lender, not the borrower. Do not use a consumer loan or an informal lender for a business these schemes can finance, and do not pay an agent to arrange a MUDRA loan, because the application is made at the bank.

tips.title: There is no fresh-graduate quota in Indian recruitment: eligibility turns on age, degree and attempts, and some state police boards give weight to NCC or sports certificates
tips.cost: Free. Read the advertisement before you sign a contract or accept a post, because eligibility is decided on the cut-off date in the notification.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian government recruitment does not reserve posts for recent graduates the way some systems do. Eligibility is age, educational qualification and, for the civil services, the number of attempts, all fixed in the notification. What can change the odds is a certificate: an NCC certificate or a state or national level sports certificate carries weight in some state police and paramilitary recruitment, and the advertisement says how much. Signing a private job contract does not disqualify you from a government examination, because there is no status to lose.
tips.benefit: The rules are in the advertisement, and they are few. The Civil Services Examination requires a bachelor's degree and an age within the band the notification sets for your category, with a fixed number of attempts for the general category and more for the reserved categories; the Staff Selection Commission's recruitments set a qualification per post, from class 10 for some Group C posts to a degree for others. A person in a private job may apply, and no rule says that a contract or a provident fund account bars a government examination. What does carry weight in some recruitments is a certificate: several state police boards award marks for an NCC certificate or for representing the state or the country in sport, and the advertisement states the marks. The defence services have separate graduate entries, and those are separate competitions.
tips.sources: Union Public Service Commission. <https://upsc.gov.in/>; Staff Selection Commission. <https://ssc.gov.in/>; Ministry of Education. <https://www.education.gov.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Grade A because the eligibility rules are published, but the weight for NCC and sports certificates differs by state and by recruitment, and a certificate that helped in one state may count for nothing in the next. Age is counted on the date in the notification, and a category certificate must be in the prescribed format. Do not accept a private job on the promise that it will not affect a future application, and do not resign from one on the promise of a government post that has not been advertised. A government post begins with the appointment letter, not with a result.
